Goal: I can prove the perpendicular from the center bisects a chord.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: a line through the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord. Converse: the perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the center.

Proof: the radii OA and OB to the ends of the chord are equal, so triangle OAB is isosceles. With M the foot of the perpendicular from O, triangles OMA and OMB are right triangles with OA = OB and OM shared, so they are congruent by HL, and AM = BM.

Broken plate: draw two chords that are not parallel; their perpendicular bisectors cross at the center.
